title: TexasState vs TTU: tuition, size, accreditation

sections.heading: How they differ
paragraphs: Texas State University and Texas Tech University Health Sciences Center El Paso (TexasState vs TTU) are both public institutions but differ significantly in size and location. TexasState has a large undergraduate enrollment of 36,177 students, whereas TexasTech's El Paso campus serves a much smaller undergraduate population of 242. TexasState is located in San Marcos, while TexasTech El Paso is situated in El Paso. Additionally, TexasState provides an in-state tuition rate of $11,450, while TexasTech El Paso does not list an in-state tuition figure. These differences highlight the distinct scale and setting of each university.

sections.heading: Cost
paragraphs: Cost is a significant factor when comparing Texas State University and Texas Tech University Health Sciences Center El Paso (TexasState vs TTU). TexasState offers an in-state tuition rate of $11,450 and an out-of-state tuition rate of $22,930. In contrast, TexasTech El Paso does not provide specific tuition figures for either in-state or out-of-state students. Regarding student debt, the median debt for completers at TexasState is $21,000, which is notably higher than the $12,500 median debt reported for TexasTech El Paso graduates. These financial differences reflect the varying structures and programs offered by each institution.

Overall, TexasState vs TTU shows that while Texas State University has clear tuition rates for residents and non-residents, Texas Tech University Health Sciences Center El Paso's costs are less transparent. The disparity in median debt suggests differences in program length, cost, or financial aid availability between the two universities.

sections.heading: Pick TexasState if
paragraphs: Pick Texas State University if you prefer a public institution with a high admission rate and more accessible entry. These factors make Texas State University a suitable choice for students seeking a public university with relatively open admissions and manageable tuition costs.
